summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable (steady_2d_relevant=false). Both gates failed: input_gate_pass=false because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and scientific_gate_pass=false. Studio did not run: simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed=false, and no artifacts exist. The scenario is the two-core Alpha 21264 proactive memory-based computing (MBC) experiment in Table III (bitcount paired with swim). The experiment kind was declared custom_2d_steady, but it has an empty floorplan and no power, so it carries no transient trace and could not represent the paper's workload-driven behavior. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes, powers, source commit, or generated placement were used, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was produced. The final verdict is gated off and comparison_valid=false. The paper reports a peak integer ALU temperature of 79.14 C (No MBC) falling to 71.88 C (MBC A25) from gem5, McPAT, and HotSpot 2.0, sampled every 50,000 CPU cycles. With no Studio output, no numerical comparison to these values is made, and none would be valid. Location (integer ALU sub-unit), aggregation (run peak), regime (transient, controller-dependent), and boundary assumptions (unspecified HotSpot package) would not match a block-level steady Studio result. Only a qualitative remark is possible: the paper attributes the temperature reduction to moving computation from the ALU to cache lookup tables, which a static 2D thermal solver cannot represent apart from changes in power input. Exact replication is not claimed.

The controller is a microarchitectural technique (proactive memory-based computing with a Central MBC Optimizer and reconfigurable cache partitioning) that moves computation from the ALU to cache LUTs. A static 2D thermal solver has no representation of it; its effect enters only through gem5/McPAT time-varying power. It cannot be reproduced from block dimensions and watts.

The result is transient, workload-driven ALU temperature, sampled every 50,000 cycles. A steady-state or one-row power trace would not reproduce the transient peak, and the paper publishes no power time series.
The temperature is for the integer ALU sub-unit inside Alpha 21264 cores. The paper gives no sub-block floorplan, so a Studio model at core or block level cannot resolve the observable.

No block dimensions, coordinates or per-block power are published (only 'Alpha 21264 cores placed side by side'). The paper does not state HotSpot package, cooling or material parameters. Total power would have to be invented or split without a published rule.
The setup involves no 3D stack, interposer or chiplet system. Cooling and package details for HotSpot 2.0 are unspecified, so any Studio package would differ from the original.

Performance and reliability coupling (execution-time overhead of 1.00–1.21, L2 contention across cores, cache miss effects) is part of the paper's optimization objective and is not captured by a thermal-only solver.
The paper-linked and packet asset lists are empty, so no Studio package or material assumptions are documented in the packet and none are taken from it.

If an illustrative 2D placement is built, it would be a separate runner construction with generated coordinates and a single-row power trace. It must not be treated as paper-derived and its temperatures must not be compared numerically to the paper's 79.14 degC.
Exact replication of the paper's gem5/McPAT/HotSpot MBC experiment is not claimed.
